title: Play deadSPEAKER, inc. on RUN.world
author: lthrjcktjckr
selftext:
a horror-comedy puzzle game created for the [run.world](http://run.world) 'back to work' jam. it's based on a worldbuilding concept my brother & i developed after he told me about a dream he had where he was working a call center job, & keenly aware the caller on the other end of the line had died a long time ago, so helping her troubleshoot remotely was going to be extra challenging



the game was assembled entirely on the run platform, which uses phaser. their in-house client/agent/tools (i was a creative writing major, essentially zero coding/programming knowledge, 2006 myspace html notwithstanding)

when the theme got revealed, my brain immediately went to that dream. so first, i gave gemini the concept & with it iterated a few gdd's

then, assets were usually first iterated via google flow, pixelcut to x the background, open in picsart to manually adjust, add effects, paint over manually, or combine multiple elements 

i put care into the visuals, visual cohesiveness & imo a relatively unique & consistent aesthetic (definitely not one everyone will love, but it's very much a reflection of my brain, (in my brain, capitalism = black magick death cult, so i like a neon corporate-occult, corporate logo = sigils vibe)

the gameplay: i struggled getting agents to fully translate the environmental storytelling intended. when telling the agent that it should be visually obvious to players what to do, the ai repeatedly translated that sentiment as "include onscreen step-by-step text instructions" which is very much the opposite of the goal. for the most part, i think i've gotten most of its attempted hand-holding out of the way. ultimately, it's intended to be eerie vibes & esoteric/gnostic occult lulz & maybe the engine has strict rules, i know they're there in the initial gdd gemini whipped up based on my concept+prompt, but i have no idea what's going on or what i'm supposed to be doing when playing it, & that's sort of the point. the gameplay/ui is based on my own very brief but legit traumatic stint at time warner cable using a certain ICOMS billing system. which is to say, it's a little overwhelming, heavy on the 2000s jank, but (to me at least) also a but hauntingly nostalgic



oh, i did custom design most of the the (non-pre-existing) sigils (witch 👋) and also all of the music is hand-composed by me, assorted midi instrumentals that matched the vibe and haven't been turned into (my true passion) catchy, depression pop

thanks for checking it out xo
